key_idea: The proof achieves constant rate, distance, and locality by constructing codes on the squares of a Left-Right Cayley complex, which looks locally like a tensor product of codes (enabling testability) while being a global expander (ensuring rate and distance).
reason: The proof solves a monumental open problem through a brilliant, unexpected unification of algebraic topology, geometric group theory, and coding theory. While it requires a formidable tower of technical machinery and intermediate lemmas, the argument remains entirely conceptual and the sheer explanatory power of the central topological construction shines through.
recognized: Dinur, Evra, Livne, Lubotzky, Shahar (2022), Locally Testable Codes with constant rate, distance, and locality
